findings.claim: ADR-0016 picks case A/B/C from `agent_type` in the hook payload. Gemini CLI hook payloads carry no subagent field, so the Gemini row (line 41: case A yes, rewrite supported) cannot tell a subagent call from a main call.
findings.evidence: gemini-cli@51617c1 packages/core/src/hooks/types.ts:141-147 HookInput = {session_id, transcript_path, cwd, hook_event_name, timestamp}; hookEventHandler.ts BeforeTool input adds only tool_name, tool_input, mcp_context, original_request_name. Scheduler knows `subagent` (scheduler/scheduler.ts:124,649) but passes it only to checkPolicy, not to evaluateBeforeToolHook (scheduler.ts:616, hook-utils.ts:43-48). Subagent tool calls still fire hooks (agents/agent-scheduler.ts:64 -> Scheduler -> evaluateBeforeToolHook). Built-in subagent codebase_investigator has tools LS, READ_FILE, GLOB, GREP only (agents/codebase-investigator.ts:119-124): no shell, no MCP.
findings.fix: Add a Gemini row to the 'How the subagent's tools are known' section: identity unknown on Gemini, so every Gemini call must use an alternative that every context can call (case C style: AfterTool deny with chunks in the reason text, Read with offset/limit), or add a live check that proves otherwise. Do not mark Gemini case A/B as decided per subagent.

findings.claim: 'Gemini … block the tool when a hook fails' is wrong for the common failure. A Node crash exits 1 with a stack on stderr; Gemini turns exit 1 into allow + warning. Only exit codes >= 2 block. A timeout gives success:false, not a block.
findings.evidence: gemini-cli packages/core/src/hooks/hookRunner.ts:42 EXIT_CODE_NON_BLOCKING_ERROR = 1; :541-558 exit 0 -> allow, exit 1 -> {decision:'allow', systemMessage:'Warning: …'}, other non-zero -> deny; :454-471 non-JSON stdout/stderr goes to convertPlainTextToHookOutput; :436-447 timeout -> success:false.
findings.fix: State the Gemini rule exactly: exit 2+ or non-JSON text with exit 2+ blocks; exit 1 fails open. Keep 'hooks must never throw', and add a GP3 case: hook exits 1 -> tool runs, exits 2 -> tool blocked.

findings.claim: The doc says only server `instructions` are lost in untrusted folders. In fact Gemini does not start any MCP server in an untrusted folder, while extension hooks still run. With folder trust on by default, an unknown folder is untrusted, so ctx tools are absent while BeforeTool still fires.
findings.evidence: packages/core/src/tools/mcp-client-manager.ts:461-463 and :576-578 `if (!this.cliConfig.isTrustedFolder()) return;`; hooks/hookRegistry.ts:180-196 project hooks skipped when untrusted, extension hooks always processed; cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts:1916-1920 folderTrust.enabled default true; core/src/config/config.ts:3204 `return isTrusted ?? false`.
findings.fix: Rewrite the row: 'untrusted folder = no context-mode tools at all'. Add a GP3 golden case for Gemini: no ready row (ADR-0008 #4) -> hook never denies with a ctx alternative. This repeats the #794/#1037 dead end otherwise.

findings.claim: v2 does not say how the Gemini row handles external MCP servers (#529) or how it tells its own server apart. The v1 Gemini matcher `mcp__(?!.*context-mode)` matches nothing on Gemini (mcp_ single underscore). The Gemini payload has `mcp_context.server_name`, which gives the server without parsing the name.
findings.evidence: gemini-cli packages/core/src/tools/mcp-tool.ts:32 separator '_', :37 prefix 'mcp_', :725-731 generateValidName; hooks/types.ts:481-483 McpToolContext {server_name, tool_name}; hookPlanner.ts:104-113 matcher is `new RegExp(matcher)`. v1 configs/gemini-cli/settings.json BeforeTool matcher ends in `mcp__plugin_context-mode` (also wrong shape). tickets/v2-test-ledger.md:119 #529 -> GP3 hooks.
findings.fix: In the Gemini adapter row: matcher prefix `mcp_`, decide own-vs-external from `mcp_context.server_name === 'context-mode'` (exact compare, no regex decision), and add #529 golden cases built from a recorded Gemini payload.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY 3900db8c 2026-05-12 'feat(gemini-cli): route external MCP tools through PreToolUse (closes #529 partial — gemini-cli)'. ORIGINAL_INTENT: "slack / telegram / gdrive / notion-style MCPs trigger the context-guidance nudge before their large payloads flood the model's context window"; shape taken from hooks/core/tool-naming.mjs:21 `mcp__context-mode__${tool}` (never live-checked). REGRESSION_RISK: dropping external-MCP routing re-opens #529 on Gemini; copying the v1 pattern keeps it silently broken. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: keep the #529 intent, use `mcp_` and server_name, test against recorded payloads (#1222 rule).

findings.claim: GS5 says 'The repo has no SKILL.md', but §3.9 [D 2026-10-14] ships `skills/` with three SKILL.md files that the Gemini extension loads.
findings.evidence: TECH-SPEC.md:38 GS5 vs :207-208 'One source dir skills/ (3 files)'; drafts.md:62-69 skill_ctx-stats. Gemini loads `<extension>/skills` (cli/src/config/extension-manager.ts:924-925).
findings.fix: Change GS5 to 'no SKILL.md outside skills/ (exactly the 3 ctx-* files)'.

findings.claim: S-SKILLS is open for Gemini, but source answers it: Gemini turns every skill into a slash command and ignores `disable-model-invocation`, so the model can also activate /ctx-stats etc. through activate_skill.
findings.evidence: cli/src/services/SkillCommandLoader.ts:29-41 skills -> slash commands named skill.name; core/src/skills/skillLoader.ts:43-49 frontmatter reads only name + description; grep for 'disable-model-invocation' in core/src/skills and SkillCommandLoader: 0 hits; tool-names.ts:20 ACTIVATE_SKILL_TOOL_NAME.
findings.fix: Mark Gemini [V] in §3.9: `/ctx-stats` works from `<ext>/skills`; model invocation cannot be turned off, so skill bodies must stay harmless when the model calls them (they are).

findings.claim: §6.9 still lists Gemini as a 'required' live cell with GEMINI_API_KEY. Owner decision: no API keys for tests. ADR-0012 supersedes it but §6.9 is not marked, and ADR-0012 runs only claude and codex, so the open Gemini live checks (S-NAMES mcp_ check line 395, compaction, ADR-0016) have no runner.
findings.evidence: TECH-SPEC.md:351 header '### 6.9 Live E2E job … [D: no nightly]', :361 GEMINI_API_KEY; :395 'live check of the Gemini mcp_ finding'; adr/0012-keyless-live-harness.md:17 'only claude and codex. The others are not installed and print SKIPPED'.
findings.fix: Mark §6.9 superseded by ADR-0012 in place. Add a Gemini keyless path (Google login in a temp GEMINI_CLI_HOME, like Codex auth.json symlink) or downgrade Gemini to source-verified with the risk named.

findings.claim: PRD §15.3 says only four canonical events are used and 'Not used: PreCompact'. ADR-0009 §6 needs a compaction hook on Gemini (PreCompress) to write pending_compact. Gemini has no SessionStart on compaction.
findings.evidence: adr/0009-compaction-and-memory.md:96; gemini-cli hooks/types.ts:51 PreCompress, :607-611 SessionStartSource = startup|resume|clear only; context/chatCompressionService.ts:491-493 fires PreCompress before compression.
findings.fix: Add PreCompress to the Gemini column (and the same for Copilot CLI, VS Code) or note in §15.3 that ADR-0009 adds a fifth event for these agents.

findings.claim: The Gemini update step removes only the v1 MCP entry. v1 hooks in ~/.gemini/settings.json (`context-mode hook gemini-cli …`) keep firing next to the extension's hooks until ctx_upgrade runs, so every tool call is hooked twice. A second install also fails if an extension named context-mode exists.
findings.evidence: v1 configs/gemini-cli/settings.json BeforeTool/AfterTool/AfterModel commands `context-mode hook gemini-cli …`; gemini-cli hookRegistry.ts:170-196 merges settings hooks and extension hooks; extension-manager.ts:314-316 'is already installed. Please uninstall it first.'
findings.fix: Make the documented order: remove v1 hooks and MCP entry (or run ctx_upgrade from the new install at once), then install; use `gemini extensions update` when already installed. Add an E2E case: v1 settings + v2 extension -> each hook fires once after upgrade.
